prompt.es: Escribe un texto que compare dos fiestas con matices, una generalización y un ejemplo.

answer.text: The spring parade in Ana's city and the harvest fair in Tom's town are quite different, but both are lively. The parade is far more crowded than the fair: thousands of people come to see the colourful costumes and listen to loud music. The fair, in contrast, is nowhere near as noisy, because it has only about two thousand visitors and gentle music. The parade is also noticeably older; it is about two hundred years old, whereas the fair is only fifty. In both places, families tend to spend the day together and share food. For instance, Tom's grandmother prepares the same soup for the fair every year. Of course, not everybody follows this custom, and many visitors simply enjoy the music. In short, each festival has its own character, and neither is better than the other.
accepted: The spring parade in Ana's city and the harvest fair in Tom's town are quite different, but both are lively. The parade is far more crowded than the fair: thousands of people come to see the colourful costumes and listen to loud music. The fair, in contrast, is nowhere near as noisy, because it has only about two thousand visitors and gentle music. The parade is also noticeably older; it is about two hundred years old, whereas the fair is only fifty. In both places, families tend to spend the day together and share food. For instance, Tom's grandmother prepares the same soup for the fair every year. Of course, not everybody follows this custom, and many visitors simply enjoy the music. In short, each festival has its own character, and neither is better than the other.

Ana's spring parade and Tom's harvest fair are similar in some ways, but they are not the same. The parade is much bigger and slightly more expensive than the fair, and its costumes are far more colourful. However, the fair is every bit as friendly, and many visitors say it is more relaxed. Generally, families tend to cook and eat together during both festivals. For example, Ana's cousins make the same dish every spring, whereas Tom's neighbours bring bread to the fair. Not all families do this, of course, but it is a common custom. Both festivals show that traditions change from place to place, and that one festival is not better than another.

I compared two festivals: the spring parade in Ana's city and the harvest fair in Tom's town. The parade is far older than the fair, whereas the fair is slightly cheaper for families. The fair is not quite as crowded as the parade, but it is every bit as lively when the music starts. Many people in both places tend to wear special clothes and meet relatives. For instance, Tom's grandmother makes soup for the whole village, and Ana's neighbours dance in the street. These are only examples, and not everybody does the same. In general, both festivals are different ways of celebrating the same idea: being together.

feedback.es: El texto presenta las dos fiestas, las compara con far, nowhere near as o slightly, generaliza con tend to y respalda la idea con un ejemplo concreto.

origin.text: Datos. Fiesta A: desfile de primavera de la ciudad de Ana: miles de personas, trajes de colores, música fuerte, unos 200 años de antigüedad. Fiesta B: feria de la cosecha del pueblo de Tom: unas 2.000 personas, música suave, comida en familia, unos 50 años de antigüedad. Escribe entre 110 y 170 palabras: usa dos comparaciones con matiz (far, slightly, nowhere near as… as), una generalización con tend to y un ejemplo concreto con for instance.
